title: Your Phone Is Dirtier Than a Toilet Seat
description:
When did you last clean your phone? 🤢

• University of Arizona microbiologist Charles Gerba found phones can carry about 10x more bacteria than most toilet seats.
• Why: toilet seats get cleaned all the time; phones almost never.
• A CU Boulder laser study showed a lidless public toilet flush sends an invisible aerosol plume up to about 5 feet high within 8 seconds.
• Good news: most microbes on a phone are harmless. A wipe with a microfiber cloth helps.

Sources:
- LiveScience (2012), Why your cellphone has more bacteria than a toilet seat: https://www.livescience.com/22822-cell-phones-germs.html
- TIME (2017), Your phone is covered in germs: https://time.com/4908654/cell-phone-bacteria/
- Colorado Sun (2022), CU Boulder toilet plume study: https://coloradosun.com/2022/12/09/public-toilets-bathrooms-flushing-bacteria-public-health/
- Down To Earth (2022), the plume captured with lasers: https://www.downtoearth.org.in/health/toilets-spew-invisible-aerosol-plumes-with-every-flush-here-s-the-proof-captured-by-high-powered-lasers-86452

questions.q: Is your phone dirtier than a toilet seat?
questions.a: It can be. University of Arizona microbiologist Charles Gerba found phones can carry about 10 times more bacteria than most toilet seats, because toilet seats get cleaned and phones almost never do.

questions.q: How much bacteria is on a phone?
questions.a: About 10 times more than most toilet seats, according to Charles Gerba's research. Most of those microbes are harmless.

questions.q: How do you clean your phone safely?
questions.a: Wipe it regularly with a microfiber cloth, and keep it out of the bathroom: a lidless toilet flush can send an invisible plume up to about 5 feet high within 8 seconds.
